stemMd: Why does the author contrast cheap and expensive parts?

options.label: A
options.textMd: To argue that all inventory is wasteful.

options.label: B
options.textMd: To recommend buying only the cheapest equipment.

options.label: C
options.textMd: To show delivery time is irrelevant.

options.label: D
options.textMd: To show that purchase price alone is a poor guide to the value of holding a spare.

options.label: E
options.textMd: To prove expensive parts never fail.

explanationMd: A cheap part may prevent an expensive shutdown, while a costly part may be quickly obtainable when needed. The contrast separates unit price from the operational consequences of absence.

distractorRationale.e: No failure-rate claim of that kind is made.
distractorRationale.b: The decision concerns spares, not all equipment purchases.
distractorRationale.c: Delivery time is a central criterion.
distractorRationale.a: Some spares are justified by interruption costs.
